newsitem.title: RUSSIA: LUKoil seen good long-term performer.
newsitem.headline: LUKoil seen good long-term performer.

text.p: Preliminary results for 1996 from Russia's largest oil company on Wednesday show LUKoil poised for clear long-term growth although the share price may only track the market this year, analysts said.
"If anything in the Russian oil sector is laying the foundation for future growth, it's LUKoil," said Per Maelstrom, head of research at Brunswick brokerage, which recommends the shares.
"But the full results of this will not be seen until the end of 1998 or the beginning of 1999."

OAO Neftyanaya Kompaniya LUKoil said its 1996 net profit had risen to over three trillion roubles ($535.1 million) from 2.4 trillion in 1995, according to Russian accounting standards, which are intended as a basis for tax calculation rather than investment consideration.
The integrated oil company has calculated its proven oil reserves to be 10.5 billion barrels, about the sixth largest among world oil companies.
LUKoil is one of the most open Russian companies and is a favourite with emerging markets investors.
LUKoil's crude oil production rose to 58.3 million tonnes in 1996, according to the preliminary figures, from 57.3 million in 1995. It predicted 1997 production would be 59.7 million tonnes.

The latest profits statement clarified remarks by LUKoil President Vagit Alekperov who warned of the impact of development costs and said on Tuesday that LUKoil's net profit in 1996 was 1.3 trillion roubles.
Net profit for the parent company alone, excluding subsidiaries, was 1.3 trillion roubles after 330 billion in 1995, the statement said.
A Western oil analyst in Moscow said the new figures did not offer a complete picture and that profits could be disappointing.
"I have read their explanation, but they haven't supported it with figures. There is still a lot of uncertainty as to what the US GAAP (international accounting standard) results will be."
Brunswick said it expected the total net profit to U.S. GAAP for 1996 to be just over $700 million. It gave no comparison.

International auditors KPMG are preparing LUKoil financial statements to international accounting standards as the company prepares for an international share placement in New York this year. It has already issued American Depositary Receipts.
Renaissance Capital investment bank recommended LUKoil as a long-term buy but said the preliminary profit levels, if confirmed, could negatively affect the share price.
Like all leading companies in the Russian equities market, LUKoil's shares have soared in the last two weeks, rising to $13.20 during afternoon trade on Wednesday from about $10.70 before Christmas.
Renaissance noted LUKoil had performed exceptionally strongly in the recent shares rally.

"However, with the possibility that profitability has stagnated for the time being, higher relative valuations and a possible $1 billion share offering looming at year-end, we anticipate that LUKoil will track the market for most of 1997," it said in a statement.

Maelstrom said that LUKoil's stock performance could end the year in the range of $12-$20 per share, depending on the development of the Russian share market, which at present gives a high premium to liquid shares such as LUKoil.
"LUKoil is still undervalued over the long term," he said. "(But) we do not expect the market price to move very quickly from here." ($ = 5606 Russian Roubles)
